q: Our electricity bills are still in the old company name after a merger. Can we count them?
title: Bills in an old company name
short: Yes. What matters is that the site sits inside your reporting boundary, not the name printed on the bill. Keep the merger or name-change document next to the bills, and recalculate your base year if the merger brought in a large new site.
audience: MSMEs after a merger, takeover or name change

ul: The board resolution, merger order or name-change certificate.
The consumer number on the bill, matched to the site you now run.

p: A merger is a structural change. If it shifts your total materially, the GHG Protocol asks you to restate the base year as if the site had always been yours.

senseible: Senseible keeps each figure tied to its invoice, factor and method version, so a verifier can trace any number back to the document it came from.
